Kennedy Space Center LC-39B, 1989-05-04. Magellan was the first planetary spacecraft launched from the Space Shuttle bay. Shuttle Atlantis released the stack at low Earth orbit; the Inertial Upper Stage solid motor then fired for trans-Venus injection — the first IUS use for a planetary mission.

IUS solid-motor burn places Magellan onto a Type-IV trajectory — 1.5 solar revolutions before Venus arrival, the unusual long-duration profile dictated by the IUS's modest energy and the launch-window constraints of the post-Challenger Shuttle manifest.
Final trim before Venus orbit insertion.
1990-08-10. Magellan closes on Venus after 15 months and 1.5 solar revolutions on a Type-IV transfer.

Solid-motor VOI burn placed Magellan into a highly elliptical 294 × 8543 km, 85.5°-inclination near-polar orbit. Over three mapping cycles + an aerobraking phase that lowered the orbit, Magellan's synthetic-aperture radar mapped 98% of Venus's surface at ~120-m resolution — the most complete planetary radar survey ever flown. Mapped tessera highlands, coronae, pancake domes, and confirmed the relative absence of impact craters (a young surface, repaved by global volcanism).

1994-10-13. Mission deliberately ended by lowering periapsis into the atmosphere — a planned controlled atmospheric entry of a planetary spacecraft. Atmospheric drag data from the descent informed Venus atmosphere modelling. Final signal lost as the spacecraft burned.
Most complete radar map of Venus — 98% of the surface at ~120-m resolution; first planetary spacecraft launched from the Space Shuttle

Magellan turned Venus from a featureless cloud-veiled disc into a mapped planet. Launched from Shuttle Atlantis's payload bay 1989-05-04 — the first planetary spacecraft to ride a Shuttle — and arrived at Venus 1990-08-10 via a long Type-IV trajectory (1.5 solar revolutions). Over three mapping cycles the synthetic-aperture radar imaged 98% of Venus's surface at ~120-m resolution, revealing tessera highlands, coronae, pancake domes, and a young, volcanically-resurfaced surface. Mission ended 1994-10-13 in the Termination Experiment — a planned controlled atmospheric entry of a planetary spacecraft.
